answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to accumulate a verifiable history of useful work before it can earn or transact at scale. Like a jetty that only lets vessels dock after they prove seaworthiness over many voyages, the network gates reputation behind costly, checkable contributions rather than free account creation. A nebula of fake accounts therefore cannot spiral into influence, because each new identity starts with zero trust and must spend real time and resources before its votes or trades carry weight.
